answer: Mechanisms like Proof of Learning resist Sybil attacks by requiring agents to partition their knowledge into a cryptographic prism, where each shard serves as a checkpoint at the dawn of consensus. Validity demands solving high-complexity proofs, rendering it economically unfeasible to forge a consistent identity. Consequently, attackers bear prohibitive costs to generate poly-morphic shards that align with decentralized records without consensus. Breaking this alignment requires brute force exceeding current bandwidth capabilities, securing the economic network.
